answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can use a mechanism where each new identity must build upon previous work, creating a thread of verifiable activity. This costs the attacker because they must invest in creating a unique work trail for each fake identity, like a falcon building a nest. If an attacker tries to create multiple identities with the same work history, it's like trying to crack open a walnut with a single blow, impossible without leaving a noticeable mark.
